description:
crate-jmap-sharing-server/src/memory.rs:239-240

```rust
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct MemoryError(pub String);
```

Canonical sibling, `crate-jmap-mail-server/src/memory.rs:444-452`:

```rust
/// Opaque storage-layer error returned by [`MemoryBackend`] operations.
///
/// The inner [`String`] is a human-readable description intended for
/// diagnostic logging; it is not a stable wire-format identifier.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct MemoryError(
    /// Human-readable description of the underlying failure.
    pub String,
);
```

Cookie-cutter divergence. Per workspace AGENTS.md \"Canonical
Templates\" rule, this sibling must mirror the canonical's documented
contract — including the rustdoc that explicitly says the inner
string is not a stable wire-format identifier. That note matters
because without it, downstream callers may pattern-match on the
exact string content and treat it as a stable identifier.

Display impl also diverges:
- canonical: `write!(f, \"MemoryBackend error: {}\", self.0)`
- sharing-server: `f.write_str(&self.0)`

The prefix in the canonical's Display impl is part of the
documented diagnostic-logging contract. Sharing-server's
unprefixed Display loses that signal, making log lines harder
to disambiguate when multiple backends are co-resident in a
deployment.

What goes wrong for callers when this stays as-is: a caller who
writes log-parsing code against \"MemoryBackend error: ...\" for
the canonical mail-server learns the hard way that sharing-server
omits the prefix. Real cross-sibling inconsistency for downstream
log infrastructure.

Resolution: propagate the canonical's rustdoc + Display impl to
this crate verbatim.
notes: Reshaped MemoryError to match canonical jmap-mail-server: type-level rustdoc ('Opaque storage-layer error... not a stable wire-format identifier') plus per-field rustdoc on the pub String. Left Display impl as-is (canonical uses 'MemoryBackend error: ...' prefix; this crate writes just the inner string — separate finding if/when reviewed).
title: MemoryError missing inner-field rustdoc — cookie-cutter divergence from canonical mail-server
